Temporal focus:

    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    The ECB is widely expected to raise rates 25bps to 2.50% on Sept 10, 2026, driven by an Iran-war-fueled oil/gas price surge pushing inflation back above 3%. Core inflation has eased to 2.4% and wage pressures are contained, limiting the risk of a 2022-style spiral. Markets price one more hike this year plus one or two in 2026-27; most economists see Thursday as the likely peak, though risks are skewed to further tightening. Long-term bond yields are at post-GFC highs, tightening financial conditions independently. Leadership uncertainty surrounds ECB President Lagarde and board member Schnabel.
